correctness.rationale: Disjoint integer-height slices contain (b j+1)L_P(t-j) lattice points, giving an exact convolution. Setting L_[0,a](k)=a k+1 yields n^3 coefficient ab/6, n^2 coefficient (a+b)/2, n coefficient (6+3a+3b-ab)/6; first negative iff (a-3)(b-3)>15. Put u=a-3,v=b-3, uv>=16 and AM–GM gives ab>=uv+3(u+v)+9>=49 with equality only at 7,7. For a polygon L_P=Ak²+B k/2+1, summation yields n^4=Ab/12, n^3=(4A+Bb)/12, n^2=((6-b)A+3B+6b)/12, n=(2A+(3-b)B+6b+12)/12. Pick 2A=2I+B-2 ensures positive n for b<=4, while n² positive through b<=6. For b=5 a negative n means B>2I+40 => 2A>=39, so normalized volume 2Ab>=195; triangle with B=41,I=0 attains. At b=7 the simultaneous quadratic and linear negativity conditions are contradictory; rectangle 37x4 with A=148,B=82 gives both negative at b=8 and for all larger integers. Independent symbolic summation/interpolation reproduced both formulas and witnesses; finite tests do not establish the unbounded proof.
